hints.title: Read the gradient on either side
hints.body: The plotted vertical value is the gradient of the original function. At each zero of this graph, compare its sign immediately before and after.
hints.recap: A local minimum of the original function requires a change from decreasing to increasing.
hints.pitfall: A minimum of the derivative graph is not automatically a minimum of the original function.
hints.pause: Find the zero where the derivative changes from negative to positive; distinguish a crossing from a touch.

recall.reminder: A local minimum of the original function requires a change from decreasing to increasing.

solution:
1. Translate the graph. Where the plotted derivative is negative, f decreases; where it is positive, f increases.

2. Inspect the zero crossings. At A the derivative changes from positive to negative, giving a maximum of f. At C it changes from negative to positive, giving a minimum. At F it touches zero but is positive on both sides, so there is no minimum of f there.

B and E are extrema of the derivative, and D is not a zero of the derivative. Answer C.
knowledgePattern: Read a local minimum from a negative-to-positive derivative graph crossing
